Spartan Race · state sales-tax portals · built

From 1,018 portal PDFs to one reviewable workbook

The WestMark team logged into each state's tax portal and pulled the relevant information for that state: payment pages, balance pages and filed returns. A script read every PDF, recognised which kind of page it was, lifted the figures, and wrote each one as a row that points back to its page. Nothing was netted, merged or interpreted. This page shows the route from PDF to row, and lets you open any document and see both sides.

How it was done

Six stages. Each stage keeps a count and a pointer, so any row in the workbook can be traced back to a page in a PDF.

What a row means

One row is one thing one document says: a balance the portal showed, a line in its activity list, a payment confirmation, or a figure on a filed return. Every row carries the source file and page number, the tax period it belongs to, and a comment when the parser was unsure.

Why two documents can show one payment

Several portals describe the same payment twice: once on the period's page and once in a yearly payment list. Both are kept, because the second copy is the cheapest cross-check available. The workbook marks where a payment appears in more than one file. The next layer picks one source per state before anything is added up.

Checks and limits

Where two independent documents describe the same thing, the script compared them. Where a PDF could not be read cleanly, the workbook says so instead of guessing.
